description: A four-panel composite of grey-scale scanning electron micrographs, all at the same magnification, each labelled with a 30 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner and a panel letter (a)-(d) in the top-left. The panels show the microstructure of low-density steels (LDSs) after solution treatment: (a) S0 (no solution treatment), (b) S950, (c) S1050 and (d) S1150. (a) S0 is a fine, mottled, highly heterogeneous structure in which individual grains are small, irregular and uneven in size, with numerous faint straight traces and fine fragmented features but few clearly delineated boundaries. (b) S950 already displays much coarser, equiaxed grains with well-defined boundaries and numerous straight, parallel-sided laths and stripes within grains (annealing twins), together with some fine scratch-like lines. (c) S1050 shows a further coarsened structure of large polygonal grains crossed by long straight parallel twin lamellae. (d) S1150 shows the coarsest grains of the group, with few, widely spaced, straight grain boundaries and long parallel twin bands spanning the field of view. Taken together the panels demonstrate a progressive monotonic grain coarsening with increasing solution-treatment temperature.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of sample S0 (no solution treatment), 30 µm scale bar. Fine, uneven, heterogeneous structure with small irregular grains and fragmented features; individual grain boundaries difficult to resolve at this magnification.
SEM micrograph of sample S950, 30 µm scale bar. Clearly coarser equiaxed grains with distinct boundaries and abundant straight parallel-sided laths/stripes (annealing twins) inside grains.
SEM micrograph of sample S1050, 30 µm scale bar. Large polygonal grains crossed by long, straight, parallel twin lamellae; grain size larger than in (b).
SEM micrograph of sample S1150, 30 µm scale bar. Coarsest structure of the group: few widely spaced straight grain boundaries and long parallel twin bands spanning the field of view.

observations.observation: All four panels are scanning electron micrographs sharing the same 30 µm scale bar, so grain sizes can be compared directly at the same magnification.
Panel (a) (S0) shows a fine, uneven structure with barely resolvable grain boundaries, whereas panel (d) (S1150) shows very few, widely spaced straight boundaries, indicating markedly coarser grains.

Straight, parallel-sided bands running across grains (characteristic annealing twins) become abundant and longer from (b) S950 to (d) S1150, and are essentially absent as a dominant feature in (a) S0.
The caption identifies the four panels as S0, S950, S1050 and S1150, i.e. increasing solution-treatment temperature from left/panel (a) to panel (d).
The citing text states that the microstructures of all samples exhibit a single-phase austenitic structure.

The citing text states that the S0 sample without solution treatment has an uneven grain size, with both large deformed grains and fragmented small grains from thermal deformation during rolling (Fig. 2a).
The citing text states that with increasing solution-treatment temperature the grain size gradually increases, as shown in Fig. 2b-d.
No numerical grain-size values, axis labels or legends are printed on any panel; the only printed scale is the 30 µm scale bar.
No second phase, precipitate or dark-contrast constituent is distinctly visible in any of the four micrographs; contrast is dominated by grain and twin boundary topography.
